style.ai_base_prompt: This is a real photograph captured tonight by a police surveillance drone over the city of Meridian, not a render, not an illustration, not a game screenshot. Night, between 22:00 and 05:00, overcast, no moon. Drone point of view only: aerial frames from 30 to 60 m looking down at a steep angle, ground and detail frames from a small quadcopter hovering at 0.5 to 2 m with its own hard white LED lamp as the key light. Consumer-drone image quality: 24 mm equivalent, high ISO, fine luminance grain, slight chromatic fringing on highlights, mild vignette, a little motion softness at the edges. Colour: cold and desaturated, the drone lamp white, any street lighting sodium amber or cold LED, everything outside the beam falling to true black. Mood: forensic, quiet, unsettling. Absolutely no people or faces (a single heat blob in a found thermal frame is the only exception), no text, no captions, no timestamps, no watermarks, no logos, no readable signs or number plates, no HUD or crosshair, no daylight, no dawn.
style.thermal_note: Thermal frames are long-wave infrared from the drone's FLIR-style camera in a white-hot palette: hottest surfaces pure white, warm mid-grey, cold near black, no false-colour rainbow. Soft edges and low resolution, as if a 640x512 sensor was upscaled, gentle vignette, slight noise. Timestamp-free: no on-screen data, no reticle, no temperature scale, no crosshair. A found frame shows exactly one human heat signature: a bright, blurred, featureless human-sized shape lying or curled, with no face, no clothing detail, no identifying feature of any kind -- the drones see heat, not a person. Clear and generic thermal frames show no human signature at all; warm machinery (boilers, compressors, HVAC, a torch bulb) is fine.
